turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come, sit here sir. Before you go in I will check the pressure. It is one thirty eight over eighty four, and the pulse is seventy six. Okay, doctor is free.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes yes, sit. This screen is stuck again, one second. What is the problem?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Doctor, there is ringing in my right ear. Since about one month. I don't know the exact day.
[SEG0004] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, I am his wife. It is longer than that, before Diwali, six weeks at least. And he is not saying, he gets giddiness also, he holds the wall sometimes.
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): No. No giddiness. I don't know, doctor, I never felt spinning. Only the ringing.

[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Umm, sorry, say the side again? The system just refreshed. You said one month, she is saying six weeks, so roughly four to six weeks, we will not argue the date. Which ear?
[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): Right ear only. A hissing sound. More when the room is quiet. In the workshop I hardly notice it.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Hearing also? Muffled, blocked, what?
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): A bit muffled, same right ear. Well, actually I don't know how bad. Sometimes people have to say it twice.
[SEG0010] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): At home I am repeating every sentence. TV volume he keeps very high.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any pain? Any discharge, pus, water from the ear?
[SEG0012] person_3 (PATIENT): No pain. No discharge also.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Left ear is okay? Fever? Headache? I am still waiting for this page to load.
[SEG0014] person_3 (PATIENT): Left ear is fine. No fever, no headache.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Work is what? One moment, the old visit is not opening.
[SEG0016] person_3 (PATIENT): Err, machine shop. Press machines, very loud, whole shift.
[SEG0017] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ear muffs he will not wear. I have told him so many times.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the muffs, say again? I was typing.
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): The muffs itch, so most days I don't wear them. I don't know, doctor, maybe that is the cause.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any tablets you take? Any allergy to a medicine?
[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): No allergy. Umm, chemist gave sinerizine for this ringing. Three days I took, then I left it, too much sleepiness. No other tablet I am taking.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sinerizine, that is cinnarizine, and you have stopped it. Good you told me. Smoking? Alcohol?
[SEG0023] person_3 (PATIENT): No smoking. Alcohol, one peg on the weekend, not every day. I don't know if that matters.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me look. Please turn. Right drum is intact, no wax, no redness. Left side also clear.
[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): My uncle had some ear trouble, I got worried. Is this serious? I don't know.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mm. I think this is noise-related tinnitus from the machines, but that is only my working impression. We need the hearing test before I can be sure.
[SEG0027] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Then a scan also, doctor? He is very tense.

[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not today. I am booking pure tone audiometry for Thursday morning, 8:30, with the audiologist. No need to fast. Don't put oil or drops in the ear that morning, and no earphones on the way.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): If that test comes borderline, or if the ringing does not settle over the next few weeks, we might do an MRI of the ear. I am not arranging the scan now.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Please wear the ear muffs at the shop from tomorrow, that is on you. I will see you back in two weeks with the report. Nurse, the slip please.
[SEG0031] person_1 (NURSE): Yes doctor. Sir, Thursday eight thirty, audiometry, ground floor room twelve, it is on this slip. Review with doctor in two weeks after.

spec.situation: Ringing in the right ear for a month, worse in quiet; works with loud machinery without ear protection; some muffled hearing; hearing test referral.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

features: relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

omissions.text: Patient specifically denied ever feeling spinning/vertigo ('No giddiness... I never felt spinning'); this denial is not separately recorded, while giddiness is listed as present only as a disputed family report.
Cinnarizine caused excessive sleepiness, which was the reason the patient stopped it after 3 days.
Patient reported taking no other tablets/medicines currently.
Hearing difficulty detail missing: patient said sometimes people have to repeat themselves, and wife said she repeats every sentence and he keeps the TV volume very high.
Tinnitus quality was described as a hissing sound.
Doctor explicitly said no scan/MRI is being arranged today.
Audiometry location detail missing: ground floor room 12 on the slip.
